name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Schakowsky's retirement, but Democratic nominee Biss is well-funded
Republican challenger lacks fundraising and outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The baseline's D+23 margin rests on a D+19 partisan lean and a favorable environment, and nothing in the dossier contradicts it: Biss outraised and out-reserved his Republican opponent, while outside spending against him is modest for a seat this blue. Polymarket's 95% Democratic price corroborates a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unusually weak Democratic turnout operation in a low-salience open seat could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area seat open, but the district's D+19 partisan lean makes it firmly Democratic territory. Democrat Daniel Biss enters the general election with a large fundraising advantage, roughly $2.9 million raised, while Republican John Elleson reports no reported fundraising or outside support in the data provided.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the forecast leans on fundamentals and prediction markets, both of which point strongly Democratic. Outside groups have spent modestly against Biss, but not enough to suggest a competitive race. The seat remains Safe D.
